title: Routing & batching review scratchpad
content:
Quick context: taking notes while doing a deep pass on PR #842 (routing refactor + batching changes). Goal is to reduce tail latency and make the routing policy more explicit. This is a messy refactor so lots of follow-ups.

Top-level concerns (high priority):
- correctness: ensure routing policy edge-cases still route to fallback/compatible models when variant missing
- perf regressions: measure p95/p99 before and after on small/large sequence workloads
- cache interactions: KV cache invalidation semantics when route changes mid-session

Immediate checklist while reviewing code:
- [ ] Validate route selection table: ensure deterministic tie-breaker for same score (current code uses random pick)
- [ ] Confirm all new path variables are sanitized (region, tier, model_variant)
- [ ] Ensure there are unit tests for policy precedence (region overrides customer tier)
- [ ] Add integration test that simulates model-bump with cache warmed (check KV cache hits)
- [ ] Add test for fallback policy when preferred model is out of capacity (ensure controlled retry/backoff)

Refactor ideas (non-blocking but would improve long-term maintainability):
- Extract PolicyEvaluator interface and implement 2 concrete types: StaticPriorityPolicy and HeuristicPolicy. Keep existing heuristic implementation but make tests against the interface.
- Replace ad-hoc score map with a small immutable RouteScore object (fields: model, score, capacity_tier, stable) — improves readability across modules.
- Move region-aware routing logic out of scheduler module into routing module — scheduler should only schedule requests, not decide regional preference.

Performance test plan (metrics to collect):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for text-generation 1-512 tokens workloads
- throughput (tokens/sec) under 100/300/600 concurrent requests
- KV cache hit rate (prefix matches) and bytes saved
- GPU utilization and memory spikes during warmup

Observations from local runs (notes):
- Small change in score comparator caused a 7ms p99 regression on 4k token traces when batching enabled. Suspect batch formation timing changed because of different ordering.
- When model fallback triggers, KV cache keys include model_id as prefix -> cache miss on fallback; need to normalize cache key or implement model-agnostic prefix caching.

Concrete follow-ups (assign/owners):
- Diego: prototype PolicyEvaluator interface and add unit tests (due: 2026-03-05)
- Ruth: add integration test for model-bump + warm cache scenario (due: 2026-03-08)
- Maya (me): run perf matrix on staging region eu-west-1 with 100/300/600 concurrency and upload graphs to the PR comments (due: 2026-03-09)

Rollback/mitigation plan if deployed and we see regressions:
1) Immediately revert routing change commit (keep batching changes disabled)
2) Pin routing to old policy via runtime flag (hotfix) and redeploy
3) Collect traces and Redis/kv-cache logs to identify key miss patterns

Questions to raise in PR thread:
- Was the ordering change intentional? If so, add a comment describing why deterministic vs random tie-breaker is acceptable.
- Are we comfortable with model-specific cache keys? If not, what's the intended approach for cross-model cache reuse?
- Should we expose a runtime toggle for 'prefer_local_region' to run canaries with different routing policies cheaply?

Snippets to paste in PR review (examples):
- Probable bug: comparator returns boolean not comparator int which can behave differently in JS runtime when used with sort() — suggest using a consistent three-way comparator pattern.
- Suggest adding a small utility: compareRouteScore(a,b) => { if (a.score!=b.score) return b.score-a.score; return a.stable-b.stable }

Notes to self (random):
- Keep eye on spikes during policy evaluation when batcher drains partially filled batches
- Check console dashboards: route-fallback-rate, batch-formation-delay metric (not currently hooked, add ticket)
- Make sure rollout canary only hits 1% of traffic initially and has automatic rollback on p99 increase > 10% over baseline

Draft PR comment I plan to post:
"Thanks for heavy lifting on this. Flagging a few correctness/perf items in the checklist above — main risk is ordering change affecting batching. Recommend adding targeted unit/integration tests for policy precedence and cache interactions before merging. If we want to iterate faster we can land the batching improvements behind a feature flag and keep routing changes in a follow-up where we extract PolicyEvaluator." 

End of scratchpad. Will move items into Linear tasks after PR lands.
